transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-04 15:00 UTC - Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Nexus Head of ML), Ahmed Khan (Nexus CTO), Lena Brooks (Nexus Platform)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and how cost maps to routes and models. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC requirements, SOC2/KMS, and next steps for pilot.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know we're tight on time so we will jump in, we have david from our infra team showing the console and i'll run through the cost piece as well
00:18 David: hi folks, nice to meet you, ok i'll share my screen, lemme know if anything looks weird uh sometimes the annotation on my laptop creeps in
00:35 Priya: thanks, quick context - we're exploring adding llm features to our fraud detection flows and customer support workflows, we're sensitive to latency and need clear cost controls, we currently use a mix of on-prem and gcp for data
00:55 Maya: perfect, that's what we'll focus on: per-route dashboards so you can map costs and latency to individual endpoints, and routing policies that let you prefer hosted for dev and dedicated for prod
01:12 David: ok starting on the console, top left is the org overview, token consumption time series, you can filter by route, model, region, and by tags - here i'm selecting the support-chat route to show per-route metrics
01:35 David: you can see p50/p95/p99 latencies, token counts, and cost per 1k tokens, note the cost line includes batching and caching effects, so if you had prefix cache turned on the cost per token drops
01:52 Ahmed: wait how are you calculating the cost - is that actual infra cost or our billable rate?
02:03 Maya: good q - the console shows both: estimated infra cost (a model of GPU utilization based on kernel selection and batch sizes) and your billable/retail cost. we show the split so you can see margin and optimize batching/quantization
02:18 Priya: i'm seeing a spike at 11:00 on the graph, what causes that?
02:25 David: that's a burst event - you can click into the timeline and see requests grouped by session, also shows the model variant used; sometimes a fallback to a larger model for edge cases will spike cost
02:43 Priya: fallback - is that automated? we need predictable budgets so surprises are tough
02:50 Maya: yes you can set routing policies - prefer low-cost model, but fallback to high-accuracy model if confidence < threshold. also you can set hard spend limits per-route so fallback won't exceed budget without approval
03:08 David: demoing per-route drilldown - here is embeddings-route, shows avg tokens per request, concurrency, cache hit rate (we call it KV cash in one internal log, apologies), and an attribution view that ties tokens to specific prompt templates
03:28 Ahmed: attribution view sounds useful - can we map it back to product owners?
03:33 Maya: yep you can tag routes with owners and cost centers; exports go straight to csv and into your chargeback system
03:45 Lena: our security team will ask about KMS and audit trails - how are you storing keys and what logs do you provide?
03:56 David: we integrate with customer KMS (cloud-kms and HSMs), by default keys are customer-managed for Private deployments; audit logs include token-level call traces (redacted), model version, route, and routing policy decisions
04:15 Lena: redaction - can you confirm pii never lands in logs?
04:22 David: correct, we redact request/response bodies in logs, only metadata is kept; however you can opt into encrypted request logging for narrower debugging windows with consent
04:38 Priya: what about compliance - SOC 2 and ISO?
04:44 Maya: Redwood has SOC 2 Type 2 - we'll send the security pack after this call, david will share the SOC summary and the architecture diagram for Private mode
04:56 Ahmed: for pilot we likely want hosted API dev to get going and then Dedicated in our VPC for prod, timeline is Q2 - does Redwood support full VPC private control plane?
05:10 David: yes, Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package if needed; for Dedicated we can provision reserved GPU pools within your cloud account or in our accounts with strict tenancy controls
05:25 Maya: i'll add that to next steps - david will share the VPC diagram and options
05:36 David: back to cost - here's the per-route cost breakdown table, it shows billable tokens, infra cost estimate, caching delta, and a projected monthly runrate based on current QPS. you can change model variant to see hypothetical savings with a 4-bit quantized variant
05:58 Priya: how accurate are infra cost estimates? we need to justify it to finance
06:05 David: accuracy depends on workload profile, we use kernel-level profiles and historic seq-len distribution; usually the estimate is within 7-12% for steady workloads. we recommend running a short benchmark to calibrate numbers for 1-2 routes
06:22 Ahmed: benchmark - what do you need from our side?
06:26 Maya: sample prompts, expected concurrency, dataset for latency-sensitive flows, and a proxy account to run load tests; david will provide a benchmark playbook
06:38 David: i'll also share recommended batching and quantization profiles per model; for example on seq-len 256 we recommend xform-13q4 for best cost/latency tradeoff
06:50 Priya: ok on models - does Redwood host curated open models or do we bring our own?
06:56 Maya: both, we have a model catalog with vetted variants and Redwood-verified performance profiles, and you can also pin private models in Private/Dedicated deployments
07:08 Lena: there's a question about per-route SLOs: can we set p95 targets and alerting by route?
07:14 David: yes per-route SLOs, alerting hooks (pager/slack), and automatic fallback policies if latency breaches thresholds - we support canary rollouts too
07:29 Priya: curious about data residency - some flows must stay in eu-west, can routing do region pinning?
07:36 Maya: yes you can pin routes to regions and also define fallback regions, routing rules are policy-driven
07:44 Ahmed: pricing model question: is pricing per-token flat or tiered, do we get discounts for reserved Dedicated capacity?
07:52 Maya: hosted is usage-based per token with tiered discounts, Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit discounts, and we can mix modes for cost predictability - will include sample pricing in the spreadsheet
08:05 David: quick live example - changing model variant on the route shows immediate recalculation of projected monthly spend, so product managers can play with accuracy/cost tradeoffs in the console
08:21 Priya: that projection considers caching?
08:24 David: yes it factors cache hit rate and batching; you can also simulate enabling prefix caching to see effect on token counts
08:35 Lena: we've had surprises when a small percentage of requests use much longer prompts - any guardrails?
08:42 Maya: you can set max-length caps per route and soft-fallbacks; also per-route spend caps will stop high-cost fallthroughs and alert ops
08:55 Priya: ok sounds good, can we get an exportable report for month-end billing reconciliation?
09:01 David: yes CSV/Parquet exports include token-level attribution and are ready for gl-internal chargeback pipelines
09:10 Maya: quick note on observability: console has trace hooks so you can correlate llm calls with your app traces (we support opentelemetry), and token-level cost tags map to traces
09:25 Ahmed: latency numbers - do you have p95 targets for Dedicated?
09:29 David: depends on model and sequence length, but for typical chat-gen on a 7b family on Dedicated you should see p95 under 250-350ms with our optimized kernels at moderate concurrency
09:41 Priya: that's promising, our SLA ask is 300ms p95 for support flows, that seems achievable
09:47 Maya: great, we'll include sample SLOs in the pilot plan
09:55 David: another feature - per-route quality monitoring where you tie prompt sets and evals to routes; if accuracy regresses we can alert and automatically route to a higher-accuracy model until you investigate
10:15 Priya: that's very relevant for fraud detection, thanks
10:22 Lena: infra question - for Dedicated in our VPC, who operates the GPU nodes, and how do we handle updates?
10:30 David: options: fully-managed by Redwood inside your cloud account, or customer-managed nodes with our runtime installed; updates follow a canary rollout and you can opt into maintenance windows
10:42 Ahmed: good. ok next steps?
10:45 Maya: recap - i'll send pricing + pilot proposal; david will share security pack and benchmark playbook; lena to surface QPS and expected concurrency; team to pick a pilot route (support-chat or fraud-score)
10:58 Priya: i can pick the fraud scoring route, lena will gather numbers and we'll aim to start pilot week of march 9
11:08 David: i'll put together a short checklist for access (api keys, vpc peering info) and a recommended load test script
11:18 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email, and i'll schedule the kickoff once we agree on scope
11:25 Ahmed: thanks all
11:27 End of call
